stem: A nurse is caring for a hospitalized client who has received therapeutic radioactive material. Which principle should guide the nurse's radiation-safety practices?

options.A: Minimize unnecessary exposure time, maximize distance when care permits, and use the shielding or containment measures specified for the radioactive source
options.B: Use the same precautions as for hazardous antineoplastic drugs because radioactive materials require no radiation-specific controls
options.C: Remain as close to the client as possible between care activities because distance does not affect radiation dose
options.D: Ignore the facility radiation-safety instructions once the therapeutic dose has been administered

rationale: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission identifies time, distance, shielding, and containment as core radiation-protection principles. Limiting unnecessary exposure time and increasing distance reduce dose; appropriate shielding depends on the radiation source and should follow the facility's radiation-safety instructions. Therapeutic radioactive materials also require source-specific contamination controls when applicable. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Use ALARA-based radiation-safety principles when caring for clients receiving therapeutic radioactive material: minimize exposure time, maximize distance when clinically feasible, and follow source-specific shielding/containment instructions.
source_document_title: Minimize Your Exposure — Radiation Protection Principles
source_locator: Sections 'Time, Distance, and Shielding' and 'Containment': limiting exposure time reduces dose; radiation intensity/dose decreases as distance increases; proper shielding reduces penetrating radiation; radioactive materials are contained to limit environmental spread
source_claim_supported: Radiation exposure is minimized through time, distance, appropriate shielding, and containment; specific shielding/containment must be matched to the radioactive source and radiation-safety program.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Handling Hazardous and Infectious Materials, printed p.25 / PDF p.29: follow procedures for handling biohazardous and hazardous materials; ensure safe implementation of internal radiation therapy
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — radiation-safety principles / therapeutic radioactive material
correction_summary: Retained the radiation-safety construct but removed the implication that one fixed shielding method applies to every therapeutic isotope. Reframed the answer around NRC time/distance principles plus source-specific shielding/containment and facility radiation-safety instructions.
audit_findings: A correctly combines general NRC radiation-protection principles with source-specific implementation. B incorrectly equates radiation precautions with hazardous-drug handling, C reverses the distance principle, and D disregards required radiation-safety controls. The item does not prescribe a specific shield material or fixed distance because those depend on the radionuclide and clinical program. NCSBN 2026 explicitly includes safe implementation of internal radiation therapy within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Independent adversarial review found one best answer.
